facts.statement: Powellvenator is an extinct coelophysoid theropod dinosaur that lived in the Late Triassic in northwestern Argentina.
facts.quote: Powellvenator (meaning "Jaime Powell's hunter") is an extinct genus of coelophysoid theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Triassic in what is now northwestern Argentina.

facts.statement: Fossils of Powellvenator were discovered in the Los Colorados Formation within the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin.
facts.quote: Fossils of the dinosaur were found in the Los Colorados Formation of the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin.

facts.statement: The only known species, Powellvenator podocitus, was named by Martín D. Ezcurra in 2017.
facts.quote: The type and only known species is Powellvenator podocitus, named by Martín D. Ezcurra in 2017.

facts.statement: Powellvenator podocitus was described in 2017 based on partial hindlimb remains from the Los Colorados Formation.
facts.quote: Powellvenator podocitus was described in 2017 by Martín D. Ezcurra based on previously undescribed partial hindlimb remains from the Los Colorados Formation.

facts.statement: Argentine paleontologist José Fernando Bonaparte discovered several unknown dinosaur hindlimbs in the Quebrada de los Jachalleros valley in 1969.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo argentino José Fernando Bonaparte descubrió varias extremidades traseras de un dinosaurio desconocido en el valle de la Quebrada de los Jachalleros en 1969.

facts.statement: In 1972, Bonaparte described the skeleton of a small coelophysoid found in the same valley.
facts.quote: En 1972 Bonaparte describió el esqueleto de un pequeño celofisoide encontrado en el mismo valle.

facts.statement: In September 2015, a connection was established between the earliest fossils found and the new taxon.
facts.quote: En septiembre de 2015, se estableció una conexión entre los primeros fósiles encontrados.

facts.statement: The generic name Powellvenator honors the late Argentine paleontologist Jaime Eduardo Powell and literally means "Powell's hunter".
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se le da en honor al desaparecido paleontólogo argentino Jaime Eduardo Powell y literalmente significa "cazador de Powell".

facts.statement: The specific name podocitus translates to "fast leg".
facts.quote: El nombre específico podocitus se traduce como "pierna rápida".

facts.statement: Powellvenator is known from fragmentary material, particularly partial hindlimb bones, rather than a complete skeleton.
facts.quote: Powellvenator is known from fragmentary material, especially partial hindlimb bones, rather than from a complete skeleton.

facts.statement: Ezcurra diagnosed the species using distinctive ankle and foot features, including a sigmoid posterodorsal margin on the astragalus, a rounded dorsal expansion on the astragalar body, a calcaneum with a lateral flange, and a strongly reduced metatarsal II shaft.
facts.quote: Ezcurra diagnosed Powellvenator podocitus using a distinctive combination of ankle and foot characters, including an astragalus with a distinctly sigmoid posterodorsal margin, a rounded dorsal expansion on the anteromedial portion of the astragalar body in anterior view, a calcaneum with a laterally projected flange, and a strongly reduced shaft of metatarsal II.

facts.statement: Powellvenator lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Powellvenator lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: Powellvenator lived at the end of the Triassic period, approximately between 221 and 206 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente entre 221 a 206 millones de años, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: In its original description, Powellvenator was classified within Coelophysoidea as the sister taxon to Coelophysidae.
facts.quote: In its original description, Powellvenator was recovered within Coelophysoidea and as the sister taxon to Coelophysidae.

facts.statement: The parent group of Powellvenator is Coelophysidae.
The description of Powellvenator expanded the known record of early neotheropod dinosaurs in South America, which was previously much poorer than in North America and Europe.
facts.quote: Its description helped expand the South American record of early neotheropod dinosaurs, which had previously been far poorer than the record from North America and Europe.
